drhp.business: Wakefit is a full-stack vertically integrated direct-to-consumer home and furnishings company selling mattresses, furniture and furnishings and decor under the 'Wakefit' brand. It sells through its own channels (website and COCO - Regular Stores) and external channels (online marketplaces and MBOs), reaching customers across more than 700 districts, catering to mass, masstige and premium segments.
drhp.end_markets: India domestic retail (home and furnishings); mattresses 61.35% of FY25 revenue, furniture 27.61%, furnishings 11.04%
drhp.expansion: Board approved (June 26, 2025) opening of 117 new COCO - Regular Stores in FY2027 and FY2028 across cities such as Mumbai, Noida, Bengaluru, Ghaziabad, Bhubaneshwar, Lucknow, Gurgaon on an aggregate ~180,300 sq ft; plus two internally funded COCO - Jumbo Stores in Bengaluru and new equipment/machinery at the Hosur (MF IV) furniture unit to expand the engineered-wood line (running at ~96.87% utilisation).
drhp.mdna: Product mix (mattresses dominant, growing furniture/furnishings diversification)|Shift toward higher-margin own channels (website + COCO stores)|Operating leverage and process efficiencies turning EBITDA positive and PAT positive in H1FY26|Advertising/business promotion intensity (7.56% of FY25 revenue) and courier/delivery costs|Low/negative net working capital cycle (NWC days fell from 20.44 in FY23 to 3.84 in FY25)
drhp.one_liner: Largest D2C home and furnishings company in India by revenue in Fiscal 2024, offering mattresses, furniture and furnishings under the 'Wakefit' brand across an omnichannel network.

market_position.basis: Largest D2C home and furnishings company in India by revenue from operations in Fiscal 2024 (Redseer); among top three in organized mattress market; only D2C player scaled across all three categories. Spans mass, masstige and premium price segments.

opportunities: Under-penetrated home & furnishings market (per-capita spend USD 24-25 vs USD 600 in US)
Shift from unorganized to organized/branded and D2C formats (organized ~29% to ~35%)
Store expansion (117 new COCO stores, COCO Jumbo format) and interior-design services
strengths: Largest and fastest-growing D2C home & furnishings brand in India (Redseer)
Full-stack vertical integration (design to manufacturing to distribution)
Majority revenue from higher-margin own channels (website + COCO stores)
Only D2C player scaled across mattresses, furniture and furnishings (each >Rs 1,000m in FY24)
Omnichannel reach: 125 COCO stores and 1,504 MBOs across 700+ districts
threats: Fragmented, low-barrier, largely unorganized competition and price pressure
Larger organized competitors with greater resources and brand recognition
Raw-material/import price and FX volatility; regulatory (Furniture QCO 2025 / BIS) compliance
weaknesses: History of net losses (FY23-FY25) and negative operating cash flow in FY23
Revenue concentration in mattresses (61.35% of FY25 revenue)
Past internal-audit non-compliance (FY24) and auditor CARO/audit-trail remarks

concerns_observed: History of net losses in FY23-FY25 (FY23 PAT loss Rs 14,568.3 lakhs) and negative operating cash flow in FY23; sustainability of H1FY26 profitability not yet proven over a full year.
Revenue concentration in mattresses (61.35% of FY25 revenue) and in own channels/single 'Wakefit' brand.
High employee attrition (47.33% in FY25) and CFO resignation effective Dec 31, 2025.
Governance/compliance flags: no internal auditor in FY24 (suo moto adjudication filed), CARO/audit-trail remarks FY23-FY25, and delays in statutory dues (GST a subsisting default).
Offer is OFS-heavy (46.75m shares) relative to a Rs 3,771.78m fresh issue; net proceeds unappraised with broad management discretion and no orders placed/store locations identified.
data_gaps: Post-offer promoter holding and dilution % (number of fresh shares to be finalised at Offer Price).
Customer and supplier concentration percentages (not disclosed in tables).
Trade-receivables ageing beyond one year (raw amount not stated).
Debtor/inventory/creditor days split (only net working-capital days disclosed).
monitorables: Quarterly PAT/EBITDA margin trajectory and whether full-year FY26 stays profitable.
Pace and unit economics of the 117 new COCO stores and two COCO - Jumbo stores; store closures.
Own-channel vs marketplace revenue mix and marketing spend as % of revenue.
Employee attrition and KMP stability (new CFO).
Engineered-wood line utilisation (96.87% at Sep-25) and realised capacity after new machinery.
open_questions: Is the H1FY26 profitability sustainable across a full fiscal year given festive-season seasonality skewing H2?
What is the expected profitability and payback of the new COCO - Jumbo (50,000-200,000 sq ft) large-format stores, a format with no prior operating experience?
What drove employee attrition to 47.33% in FY25 and how will the incoming CFO transition be managed?
How will BIS/Furniture (Quality Control) Order 2025 compliance (effective Feb 13, 2026) affect furniture costs and product availability?
Post-offer promoter holding and lock-in following 43.01% pre-offer stake and promoter participation in the OFS?

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue CAGR ~24.87% FY22-FY24 (Redseer); FY25 revenue Rs 127,369.1 lakhs, growth 29.13%; largest D2C player in category.
EBITDA margin turned positive (7.13% FY25, 14.25% H1FY26); PAT negative FY23-FY25 but positive Rs 3,557.4 lakhs in H1FY26.
Nil borrowings at Sep 30, 2025; net worth Rs 55,733.6 lakhs; lease liabilities Rs 2,769.89m the main obligation.
Positive CFO in FY24, FY25 and H1FY26 (Rs 7,879.7 lakhs); negative CFO Rs 2,046.3 lakhs in FY23.
Net working capital days fell to 3.84 (FY25) and 1.04 (H1FY26); negative NWC of Rs 42.69m at Sep-25 (supplier-funded).
Mattresses 61.35% of FY25 revenue; own channels 56.97%; single brand; three categories diversifying.
9-member board with 5 independent directors, but FY24 internal-audit lapse, CARO/audit-trail remarks and statutory-dues delays.
RoNW -6.72% FY25 (6.38% H1FY26); RoCE -0.68% FY25; peer Sheela Foam RoNW 2.98%.
Aggregate against Company Rs 3,696.4 lakhs; contingent liabilities Rs 808.1 lakhs (Sep-25); no promoter proceedings.
Objects are retail leases, store capex, machinery and marketing; unappraised, GCP undisclosed, no orders placed.

red_flags: No internal auditor appointed in FY2024 (Section 138 non-compliance); suo moto adjudication filed, penalty outcome pending.
Auditor CARO/Rule 11(g) remarks across FY23-FY25 (audit trail absent, bank returns not agreeing with books, cash losses, statutory-dues delays).
GST is a subsisting default among statutory-dues delays (Rs 58.93m delayed in FY25).
strengths_observed: Largest and fastest-growing D2C home and furnishings brand in India by FY2024 revenue (Redseer); only D2C player scaled across all three categories, each over Rs 1,000m in FY24.
Revenue growth of 21-29% p.a. over FY23-FY25 (FY25 revenue Rs 127,369.1 lakhs), with EBITDA margin improving from -10.55% (FY23) to 7.13% (FY25) and 14.25% in H1FY26.
Turned PAT positive in H1FY26 (Rs 3,557.4 lakhs, 4.91% margin) after three loss-making fiscals; RoNW 6.38% in H1FY26 vs -6.72% in FY25.

Full-stack vertical integration and a majority of revenue from higher-margin own channels (56.97% in FY25), with a low/negative net working-capital cycle (NWC days fell from 20.44 in FY23 to 3.84 in FY25).
Effectively debt-free (nil borrowings at Sep 30, 2025) with net worth of Rs 55,733.6 lakhs; omnichannel network of 125 COCO stores and 1,504 MBOs across 700+ districts.
